name: Printing Sequence of Numbers with a Gap Between Adjacent Values (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that prints a sequence of numbers from 1 (inclusive) to 16 (exclusive) in increments of 4.
code:
#Step 1: Iterate through the numbers in the sequence
for num in range(1, 15, 4): 
    #Step 1.1: Print each number in the sequence
    print(num)

1.content: #Step 1: Iterate through the numbers in the sequence

commentList: Purpose: This line starts a loop that gives you each number in the sequence. The loop will run once for every value produced by range, and each value is placed into the variable num so you can use it inside the loop (for example, to print it).

Syntax and meaning: range(1, 15, 4) means start at 1 (inclusive), stop before 15 (exclusive), and move in steps of 4. So the generated values are 1, 5, 9, 13. The colon (:) marks the start of the indented loop body that follows.

Common errors and misconceptions: Remember the stop value is exclusive — that is why 15 is not included. Using 15 here happens to produce the same last value as using 16, but using 16 (the problem statement's exclusive bound) is clearer. If you set the step to 0 Python will raise an error, and using a step with the wrong sign can produce no iterations.

Best practices: To avoid confusion, match the problem statement by using range(1, 16, 4). Keep the print (or other body statements) properly indented under this for line so they execute inside the loop, and use a clear loop variable name if that helps readability.

3.content: #Step 1.1: Print each number in the sequence

commentList: Purpose: This line prints the current loop value so that you see each number from the sequence as the loop runs; because it's inside the for-loop, you get one output per iteration.

Syntax and semantics: print(num) calls the print function with the loop variable num as its argument, so on each iteration Python evaluates num and sends its value to standard output (by default followed by a newline).

Common errors and misconceptions: if you forget the parentheses (print num) you'll get a SyntaxError in Python 3; if you unindent this line so it's outside the loop, you'll no longer print each number (you may only print the last value or none if the loop never runs).

Best practice: keep this print inside the loop and properly indented so you print every item; if you want a different format (e.g., numbers on one line separated by spaces), consider using print(num, end=' ') or build a string and print once for cleaner output.

You might pick this because you remember that range can take two arguments and assume the loop will skip by the amount you want without giving a step. Step by step: Python treats range(1, 16) as start=1, stop=16, and uses the default step of 1. That means the loop will print 1, 2, 3, ... up to 15, not every fourth number. Using this line will produce many more numbers than intended and the spacing between numbers will be 1 instead of 4. The key problem here is the missing step argument — the line uses the default increment instead of the specific increment you needed.

commentList: You might choose this out of habit since many loops do start at 0. Step by step: range(0, 16, 4) begins at 0 and then produces 0, 4, 8, 12. That means the loop prints a 0 (which is not wanted) and misses the sequence that should start at 1. Using this line gives the wrong set of numbers because the start value is incorrect — the loop begins at 0 instead of the required first value.

That adds an extra 17 at the end, which goes beyond the intended exclusive limit. Using this line will print a number outside the allowed range, so the output includes an undesired value. The mistake is in choosing a stop value that lets the loop step one time too many.
